featured_videos.title: Keep Your Meals Simple
featured_videos.creator: Butter Bob Briggs
featured_videos.commentary: Bob and his son nailing the whole "stop overthinking it" vibe is exactly what the community needs to hear right now. I'm watching people in the Discord threads tie themselves in knots trying to nail macros, count every gram, fast for 23 hours, when what actually sticks is just, you know, cooking meat consistently and enjoying it. The comments are full of people saying this video broke them out of the prolonged fasting cycle they were stuck in, and that tracks with what I'm seeing. sometimes permission to keep it simple is the missing piece. Two people eating the same ingredients two different ways and both thriving? That's the whole game.

featured_videos.title: Carnivore Mashed Potatoes?! You Won't Believe What's in These! (No potato, no cauliflower)
featured_videos.creator: Courtney Luna
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore Mashed Potatoes?! You Won't Believe What's in These! (No potato, no cauliflower)
featured_videos.commentary: Here's the thing about recipe creativity on carnivore. it hits different when someone actually shows you the mess. Courtney's unedited blender seal disaster is more honest than a hundred perfectly filtered cooking videos, and the fact that people in the comments are already freezing these for Thanksgiving tells you this recipe actually works in real kitchens, not just Instagram ones. The egg-based approach solves a real problem for anyone who's tired of the same proteins week after week. If you're looking to add some texture variety to your meals without the usual cauliflower rebuild, this is worth the five minutes it takes to throw together.

featured_videos.title: I Tried EVERY Version Of Carnivore (Don't Waste Your Time)
featured_videos.creator: Max German
featured_videos.editorial_title: I Tried EVERY Version Of Carnivore (Don't Waste Your Time)
featured_videos.commentary: The comment section here is basically saying what I've been watching play out in the Discord for two years: people stop arguing about versions once they find what works for *them*, and that's when the real results show up. You've got someone down 229 pounds eating four foods, someone else moving between ketovore and lion depending on the day, and all of them saying the same thing. Stop waiting for the perfect formula and just start. That's the vibe that actually sticks, and it's way less sexy than "the one secret version influencers don't want you to know," but it's what people are living.

featured_videos.title: This 71-Year-Old Quit Every Medication on Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.editorial_title: This 71-Year-Old Quit Every Medication on Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: What strikes me most about Cathy's story isn't just that she's off her medications at 71. it's that she's doing hill sprints and climbing stairs like they're nothing. That's the part that matters. Most of the conversation around carnivore focuses on what you're taking away (the pills, the processed food, the constant hunger), but this video is really about what you get back: the ability to move without pain, to have energy at an age when you're supposed to be slowing down, to not feel like your body is working against you anymore. The comments are full of people in their 50s, 60s, and 70s reporting the same thing. off meds, off pain, back to living instead of managing. If you're watching this and thinking about whether a diet change is worth the effort, remember it's not actually about the diet. It's about what happens after.

featured_videos.title: This Carnivore Pizza Bowl Is All I Want to Eat
featured_videos.creator: Meet Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Carnivore Pizza Bowl Is All I Want to Eat
featured_videos.commentary: The comments hit on something real here: when you're tired after a full day, a one-pan bowl beats a complicated recipe every time. That's the actual win, not the novelty of "pizza" on carnivore. Ground beef, crispy fat, a cream sauce that tastes indulgent. those are the mechanics that matter. What I love is someone's family thought it was a cheat meal. That's the moment carnivore clicks for people around you, when the food stops feeling like a diet and starts tasting like dinner. This is the kind of simple protocol that survives a Wednesday night when you're running on empty.

featured_videos.title: This Low-carb Steak Salad Is anything But Boring!
featured_videos.creator: Becki-licious
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Low-carb Steak Salad Is anything But Boring!
featured_videos.commentary: I notice something interesting in these comments. People are talking about protocol books and systemic resets, but what they're really saying is they got tired of fighting their bodies at every meal. The steak salad video is just the hook, right? What matters is that someone showed them a real dinner that doesn't require willpower or a nutrition degree to pull together. That's where the magic actually is. I've seen this shift happen with people I coach too. they stop obsessing over what diet *should* work and start paying attention to what they can actually eat without thinking about it at 3 pm. A good steak, some greens, a vinaigrette that tastes like food instead of medicine. That's not boring. That's freedom.
